title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act prohibits the construction or operation of AI data centers on federal land. It aims to protect public property and prevent large AI infrastructure projects from taking up federal space.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 is a proposed U.S. law that aims to require companies to assess the impact of their automated decision systems on accuracy, fairness, bias, and overall societal implications. It would establish standards and reporting obligations for businesses to ensure transparency and mitigate potential harms from AI algorithms.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: This act seeks to safeguard democratic processes by limiting the use of artificial intelligence that could mislead or deceive voters. It establishes guidelines and penalties designed to prevent AI-generated misinformation from influencing election outcomes.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: This act seeks to shield families from higher utility bills caused by the growing energy use of AI data centers. It proposes measures such as subsidies, energy efficiency standards, and transparency requirements to help keep energy costs affordable.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 is a proposed federal law designed to regulate the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence technologies. It aims to set safety standards, require transparency and accountability, and protect citizens while encouraging responsible innovation.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 is a federal law that sets rules for how artificial intelligence can be built and used in the United States. It establishes safety and transparency requirements for AI developers, creates oversight mechanisms, and aims to protect privacy, reduce bias, and address national security concerns.

title: A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge announced on March 4, 2026, reflects sound national policy to protect ratepayers in the United States, promote electricity affordability, and ensure that all people of the United States, including households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms, have access to reliable and affordable energy as artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure expands across the United States.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. (text: CR S1618-1619)
summary: The resolution supports the Ratepayer Protection Pledge to keep electricity costs low for households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms. It also stresses the need for reliable, affordable energy as AI and data‑center expansion increases power demand nationwide.

title: Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025
action: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources Subcommittee on Energy. Hearings held. With printed Hearing: S.Hrg. 119-366.
summary: The Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 establishes regulations for the use of liquid cooling systems in AI hardware to improve energy efficiency and reduce environmental impact. It sets standards for safety, environmental compliance, and incentivizes manufacturers to adopt sustainable cooling technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes rules to assess, reduce, and report the environmental footprint of AI systems, including energy use, carbon emissions, and electronic waste. It requires companies to adopt sustainable AI practices, provides incentives for green innovation, and sets penalties for non‑compliance.

title: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025 is legislation that regulates how personal and non‑personal data can be used in AI systems, aiming to protect privacy, increase transparency, and promote accountability. It establishes data‑governance standards, requires clear consent for data collection, and sets penalties for non‑compliance while encouraging ethical AI development and use.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 is a proposed law that would require companies to assess and document the impact of automated decision systems, ensuring they do not discriminate or harm users. It would mandate regular audits, transparency reports, and penalties for non-compliance, aiming to protect privacy, fairness, and public trust in AI technologies.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 sets strict safety rules for AI‑powered toys made for kids. It requires manufacturers to prove that these toys meet clear safety, privacy, and ethical standards before they can be sold.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act aims to safeguard the privacy and personal data of minors who interact with AI technologies. It sets out rules for how AI systems can collect, store, and use children's data, ensuring transparency and parental consent.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act is a legislative proposal aimed at increasing the presence and representation of AI technologies across many fields. It encourages broader use and participation of AI systems in decision‑making while seeking to ensure accountability and fairness.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a framework for regulating the design, deployment, and operation of AI-powered physical systems such as autonomous vehicles, drones, and industrial robots. It outlines responsibilities for manufacturers, users, and oversight agencies to ensure safety, interoperability, and compliance with national security and public welfare standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt to the construction of new AI data centers, giving policymakers time to assess the environmental, social, and economic impacts of such facilities. This pause allows regulators to evaluate whether expanding AI infrastructure aligns with broader public interests before any further approvals are granted.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2026 establishes a framework for integrating AI topics into K‑12 and higher education curricula, aiming to equip students with foundational skills in artificial intelligence. It also sets aside federal funds for research, teacher training, and collaborative projects to promote equitable access to AI learning resources across the United States.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence‑Ready Data Act aims to set standards for collecting, cleaning, and managing data so it can be easily used by AI systems. It promotes high quality, well‑documented, and interoperable datasets that enable reliable and transparent AI applications.

title: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026
action: Star Print ordered on the bill.
summary: The Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to promote responsible development and deployment of AI technologies while safeguarding public safety, privacy, and economic competitiveness. It establishes funding for research, outlines regulatory frameworks, and encourages collaboration between government and industry to harness AI’s benefits while mitigating its risks.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act is a new regulation that sets rules for the use of AI tools in vocational education and training, ensuring they are transparent, safe, and respect privacy. It outlines obligations for educators, employers, and AI developers to protect students and maintain high quality of training.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 proposes a federal framework that requires organizations to assess and document the risks associated with AI systems before they are deployed. The act aims to protect public safety, ensure transparency, and promote responsible development and use of artificial intelligence.

title: CREATE AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The CREATE AI Act aims to establish a regulatory framework for artificial intelligence, focusing on safety, transparency, and accountability. It seeks to set standards for AI development and deployment, ensuring compliance with ethical guidelines and protecting users from potential risks.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act is a legislative proposal aimed at helping small businesses adopt and integrate AI technologies into their operations. It likely includes provisions for funding, training, and regulatory guidance to support small enterprises in deploying AI solutions efficiently.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026 aims to help small businesses understand and use AI by offering training programs, resources, and possibly financial support. It is designed to promote innovation, boost competitiveness, and reduce the skills gap in the small business sector.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a legislative proposal aimed at improving how artificial intelligence is governed and monitored. It seeks to create clear rules for AI design, use, and oversight to boost transparency, safety, and public trust.

title: Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act is a law designed to protect consumers from fraudulent schemes that use AI technology. It establishes guidelines and penalties to help ensure AI tools are used ethically and transparently in commercial and online contexts.

title: States' Right to Regulate AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act gives individual states the authority to create and enforce their own rules about artificial intelligence. It aims to let states address local concerns about AI safety, privacy, and fairness while working within the broader federal framework.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 aims to protect individuals from discrimination and bias in the use of AI systems, ensuring fairness, accountability, and transparency. It establishes legal standards for how AI technologies can be deployed and monitored to uphold civil rights and prevent harms.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 is a proposed law that would grant certain legal protections to artificial intelligence, treating AI systems as entities with rights to fair and non‑discriminatory treatment. It would also set rules for developers and users to prevent discrimination against AI and to ensure that AI technologies comply with established civil rights standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 proposes a national plan to build and support a skilled workforce for AI and other high‑impact technologies, outlining training, certification, and educational pathways. It encourages collaboration among government, industry, and academic institutions to ensure diverse, equitable access to these opportunities and to sustain the nation’s competitive edge in critical tech.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act is designed to launch a nationwide effort to inform and educate the public about artificial intelligence, its benefits, and its risks. It would create coordinated outreach programs and resources to help people understand AI and make informed decisions.

title: Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025 aims to safeguard the United States from AI systems that could pose a national security threat. It establishes regulations and oversight for foreign AI technologies, requiring disclosure and evaluation to prevent malicious use.

title: TEST AI Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The TEST AI Act of 2025 sets new federal rules for creating, using, and overseeing artificial intelligence systems. It requires companies to explain how their AI makes decisions, to evaluate and manage risks, and to put in place measures that protect privacy, safety, and fairness.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 outlines how the Small Business Administration will incorporate AI into its programs, emphasizing responsible use, transparency, and data privacy. It also establishes oversight mechanisms, accountability standards, and incentives for innovation to improve service delivery and operational efficiency.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires that any AI system capable of autonomous self‑improvement be regularly inspected and reported on by its developers to a government oversight body. It sets up a framework for tracking changes in the AI’s behavior, ensuring transparency, safety, and accountability as the system evolves.

title: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act aims to establish a systematic approach for identifying and mitigating the potential use of generative AI in facilitating terrorist planning or operations. It would require developers and users to conduct risk assessments, report findings, and implement safeguards to prevent AI tools from being abused by extremist actors.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 aims to address the environmental effects of AI systems, setting standards for reducing their carbon footprint and promoting sustainable development. It likely requires companies to report energy usage and adopt greener AI practices to protect the environment.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to restrict the use of artificial intelligence in medical diagnostics and patient care. It aims to ensure that only qualified human doctors can make critical health decisions, protecting patients from potential errors or biases inherent in AI systems.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act encourages U.S. companies to export AI technology by offering tax incentives, easing licensing requirements, and supporting research collaboration overseas. It aims to boost American competitiveness in the global AI market while maintaining national security and regulatory compliance.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act proposes laws to promote the development and sharing of AI technology through open-source platforms. It aims to foster collaboration, transparency, and responsible innovation by encouraging organizations and researchers to release AI code and models publicly.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 seeks to protect veterans by ensuring that any AI tools used in veteran services are safe, transparent, and respect their privacy and rights. The law sets standards and oversight requirements for the design, deployment, and monitoring of AI systems that affect veterans to promote fairness, accountability, and benefit.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act establishes a framework for ensuring the secure deployment of advanced artificial intelligence systems. It mandates rigorous risk assessments, continuous monitoring, and collaboration between industry, academia, and government to mitigate threats posed by AI technologies.

title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 seeks to identify and correct discriminatory patterns in AI and algorithmic decision‑making tools. It requires developers to conduct regular bias audits, disclose relevant data and model parameters, and implement safeguards to promote fairness and transparency.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a proposed law designed to protect AI models from unauthorized use and theft. It establishes legal penalties and enforcement tools so developers can better safeguard their intellectual property and prevent others from exploiting their models.
